feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete scope indicators. It reads clearly overall, but it is slightly repetitive and overpacked with overlapping skills sections, which dilutes impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope.  
- Good use of scale metrics and specifics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers), which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong positioning for public-sector digital leadership, with a rare blend of platform modernization, governance, analytics, and multimedia.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions; several bullets say what you led or built, but fewer show measurable business/user impact.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “Coleman DAVIS” is unusually capitalized; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “social, and multimedia” vs. “web, email, social and video”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education.

Spelling/grammar check: no major misspellings or grammatical errors found. Minor stylistic inconsistency: “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; use “A2 (learning)” instead.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and add scale/leadership signals from recent experience.
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented language.
- Reduce the list of functions so the intro complements rather than duplicates skills sections.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Led enterprise website transformation for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5 million annual page views, while strengthening editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader,” “platforms,” “governance,” and “content operations” overlap heavily with the subtitle and Core Competencies.
- “AI-enabled user experiences” is broad and may duplicate stronger, more specific examples in Recent Projects and current consulting work.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline, but this block currently overlaps heavily with the summary and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories slightly more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with sharper, higher-signal terms: “Digital governance, editorial workflows & CMS operations” and “Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure.”
- Consider a more concise rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance, editorial workflows & CMS operations • Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production, livestreaming & studio operations
- Keep “public-sector” hyphenation consistent and use “integrations” to match the style of adjacent items.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header and Topline Skills; keep it shorter and more category-level rather than restating detailed capabilities.
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects; “content discovery” is less repetitive.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Standardize wording and punctuation: use “10 x 20-foot” (not 10×20-foot), and keep verbs parallel (Designed, Built, Developed, Produced/Launched).
- Make outcomes more specific where possible: e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery” is good; add audience, scale, or purpose for the microsite/campaign if available.
- Trim filler like “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for ongoing campaign expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo consulting and prior NACo roles; keep the footer framed as “Selected Projects” rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it to add variety versus repeating web/platform themes.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten around consulting impact, transformation outcomes, and what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-focused phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination, publishing efficiency, and performance visibility.”
- Consolidate web build bullets: combine microsites, modular content, CMS/front-end work, and troubleshooting into one implementation bullet.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording repeats themes from “Director of Digital Media” (governance, analytics, enterprise web improvement); emphasize consultant-specific advisory and delivery work.
- “AI-enabled search” and microsite details also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel content operations.”
- Combine the strongest web metrics into one impact bullet: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add email/social growth, engagement, production volume, or campaign results if available; otherwise trim “tens of thousands/thousands” language.
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version more strategic and less operational.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as building organizational capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, cross-team coordination, and any measurable channel growth or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scope: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social, and video, scaling NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Make bullets more outcome-driven: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Produced a weekly advocacy video update that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace weak phrasing like “helped improve” with direct action: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed, and cross-team coordination.”
- Combine related bullets for concision: editorial planning + coordination across communications, advocacy, and program teams can be one stronger bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the series.
- “Digital publishing workflows” and cross-department planning overlap with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version focused on operational execution, not governance.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “content operations” to better match the senior, systems-focused positioning in recent roles.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep terminology aligned with recent experience: “governance,” “operations,” and “enterprise” are stronger than broader content-marketing phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to project and work-experience language on storytelling/editorial planning; avoid repeating both.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line focused on recent work: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop older/lower-priority items here unless central to target roles: remove WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, jQuery, and Airtable systems from this topline section.
- If you want one platform callout, keep Drupal first since it aligns with the most recent NACo work and major site migration.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing every language unless the role is explicitly hands-on developer-focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for that section.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies—avoid repeating all three verbatim across sections.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization rather than just listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped, concise wording: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing language: “KPI framework design,” “executive dashboarding,” “performance and search insights.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • SEO and digital performance insights”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory there.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational leadership and recent in-house studio/event delivery impact rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to outcomes/scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end multimedia production”
- Consider adding scale if supportable from recent roles: “Livestream and hybrid event production for advocacy programming and member events”
- Keep only 4 concise bullets; avoid overly technical terms unless they differentiate you for target roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” / “multimedia production” duplicates the Core Competencies line “Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- “PTZ camera systems” may be too tool-specific here given “Premiere Pro… Livestream studio workflows” already appears in Technical + IT

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **CMS & Web Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put **Drupal first** and add a brief qualifier since it is the most recent and most evidenced platform in your experience.
- Standardize naming: use **Microsoft Power Pages** instead of just “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats the **Topline Skills: Web Platforms & Technical Execution** entry; consider merging or removing one version.
- If kept, avoid listing the exact same five platforms elsewhere without added context such as scale, migration, or governance expertise.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere.
- Remove jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent projects; it can make the stack feel dated relative to current leadership-level work.
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a more outcome-linked capability, e.g. “serverless scripting,” “deployment automation,” or “tagging/measurement implementation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing in both places.
- API integrations and workflow automation also overlap with Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so keep this section tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and grouped to highlight systems most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first based on recent roles: Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana; move older/general collaboration tools later.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “for editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation.”
- Consider trimming to 6–7 tools max to improve signal and avoid looking like a broad but shallow list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep this item tool-specific rather than repeating the concept.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less value than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and tool-focused without repeating channel management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/enterprise weight: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional qualifiers to show depth, e.g.: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Keep to platforms only; avoid adding “email strategy” or “newsletter management” here since that impact is better shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; don’t restate outcomes here.
- “Engagement” may blur with analytics/communications competencies unless the label clearly signals platform tools.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and the Director of Digital Media entry. It should either be tightened to emphasize methods/capabilities or reduced to avoid repeating the same platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation”
- Replace vague terms like “Dashboarding” with higher-value phrasing such as “KPI design” or “executive reporting.”
- Consider changing “A/B testing” to “Experimentation” if formal testing was part of broader optimization work, not just web tests.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this stack to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing only tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; keep one more strategic and this one more tool-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating identical wording across sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful “first in-house digital team” context, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-career buildout work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outputs: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content; helped standardize day-to-day digital publishing workflows.”
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised a digital media associate’s daily production work.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/events, frequency of video series, traffic or audience growth, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the next role’s “weekly advocacy video update”; keep this item focused on launching/producing, not expanding.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated elsewhere; use “helped build early publishing processes” to distinguish it.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia/digital trajectory, but it reads generic and underplays impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, this item should stay concise and emphasize foundational achievements.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around 2 clear contributions: innovation/research coordination and first podcast launch.
- Use stronger verbs and tighter phrasing: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting program and policy teams.”
- Make the podcast achievement the headline outcome: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, stakeholders supported, or types of multimedia assets produced.

Possible rewrite
- Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.
- Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including research-based materials and program assets.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later digital media roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads like a generic software list. It should better reflect senior-level multimedia capability while avoiding overlap with the stronger “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” skills section.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize tools, not broad capabilities: **Creative & Audio/Video Tools**
- Tighten and group by function: **Adobe Premiere Pro, Audition, Photoshop, Illustrator**
